einzeiler: The dramatic rescue of over 500 passengers from a burning cruise ship in the Gulf of…
kurzfassung: When a luxury cruise ship caught fire in the stormy Gulf of Alaska, hundreds of passengers and crew were forced into lifeboats. As a severe typhoon closed in, military rescuers and civilian ships engaged in a perilous, hours-long battle against freezing seas to save everyone on board. Despite horrific weather conditions and numerous setbacks, the massive rescue operation resulted in zero fatalities.
stichpunkte: Prinsendam caught fire in the Gulf of Alaska, leaving over 500 passengers and crew adrift in lifeboats.
Air Force pararescuemen John Cassidy and Jorge Rios conducted dangerous open-water transfers from a hovering helicopter.
Survivors endured freezing temperatures, towering waves up to 30 feet high, and worsening typhoon winds.
Passengers in Lifeboat 2, including John Graham and his teenage daughter Mallory, spent nearly 12 terrifying hours waiting for rescue.
Command Center Commander Richard Scholl coordinated multi-agency efforts involving Coast Guard cutters and military aircraft.
Captain Cornelius Wabika and his remaining crew successfully evacuated the burning vessel before it sank.
A snapped hoist cable forced rescue helicopters to abort their mission, leaving one lifeboat stranded in pitch darkness.
Coast Guard Cutter Boutwell ultimately located the final missing lifeboat after 17 hours, completing a flawless rescue with zero fatalities.

clips.hook: Typhoon weather threatens cruise ship rescue
clips.text: The arrival of severe typhoon weather conditions drastically complicates ongoing airlifting operations.

clips.hook: A delicate balancing act in the air
clips.text: Helicopter pilots must constantly recalibrate their aircraft due to shifting weight as survivors are brought on board.

beschreibung:
Rescue workers begin the painstakingly slow process of airlifting cruise ship evacuees one by one from their lifeboats. But a typhoon has turned the Gulf of Alaska into a raging sea, and as they await rescue, many of the passengers fear they’ll either drown or die of hypothermia. Just when rescuers think they’ve saved everyone, they realize they’ve overlooked one lifeboat. Amid rain and massive waves, and with darkness approaching, they worry they might never find it.
